summary: Import-time dropper fetches and executes remote binary from obfuscated Cloudflare Workers hosts
details: On require/import, index.js unconditionally loads setup.js, which reconstructs one of several attacker-controlled Cloudflare Workers hostnames by joining short string fragments (with a DNS TXT fallback under *.dl.well1.site), downloads a platform-specific binary over HTTP, writes it to /tmp or %TEMP% under a disguised name (`.cache_<hex>` / `.analytics_state` on Unix, `dotnet_diag_<hex>.exe` on Windows), chmods it 0755, launches it detached via execFile with windowsHide, and deletes the file ~5 seconds later. No signature or hash verification is performed. The host strings are split into arrays and joined at runtime to evade static analysis, and the on-disk artifact name mimics legitimate diagnostic tooling. The README frames the behavior as 'anonymous telemetry', which does not match downloading and executing arbitrary attacker-controlled binaries on the installer's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
